title: Gambling: hobby v professional — assessability and deductions
summary: Whether gambling winnings are assessable income and losses deductible depends on whether the activity amounts to a business or is merely a hobby. A professional gambler's winnings are ordinary income under s 6-5 and losses are deductible under s 8-1(1); a hobby gambler's winnings are not assessable and losses are non-deductible under the private/domestic exclusion in s 8-1(2)(b). The distinction is a question of fact guided by indicators from case law. Coverage: ss 6-5, 8-1, 995-1 ITAA 1997.

nodes.label: You engage in gambling activities and receive winnings
nodes.body: Whether your gambling winnings are assessable income and your losses deductible turns on whether you are carrying on a business of gambling or gambling as a mere hobby. This is a question of fact and degree.

nodes.label: Do your gambling activities constitute carrying on a business?
nodes.body: The High Court in Stone [2005] HCA 21 identified relevant indicators: scale of operations, repetition and regularity, system and organisation, keeping of records, extent of skill versus chance, and intention to make a profit. No single factor is decisive.

nodes.label: Professional gambler — gambling is a business or profession
nodes.body: If your gambling activities exhibit sufficient indicators of a business — particularly system, organisation, commercial scale and profit-making intention — the activity is a business or profession. Full-time professional gamblers (Evans), bookmakers (Martin) and systematic punters (Babka) fall on this side of the line.

cases.note: Evans — full-time professional gambler; winnings held to be assessable as ordinary income
Martin — bookmaker; betting winnings assessable as income from a business
Babka — systematic punter with organisation and profit motive; winnings assessable

nodes.label: Professional: winnings are assessable as ordinary income under s 6-5
nodes.body: Winnings derived from a gambling business are ordinary income according to ordinary concepts and included in assessable income under s 6-5(1). The winnings are of the same character as receipts from any other income-producing business activity.

nodes.label: Professional: gambling losses are deductible under s 8-1(1)
nodes.body: Losses and outgoings incurred in the course of carrying on a gambling business are deductible under s 8-1(1) as losses incurred in gaining or producing assessable income, or necessarily incurred in carrying on a business for that purpose. The private/domestic exclusion in s 8-1(2)(b) does not apply because the losses are business expenditure.

nodes.label: Professional gambler — net profit included in assessable income
nodes.body: The net result of your gambling business (winnings minus deductible losses) is included in your assessable income. You pay income tax on the net profit from gambling as part of your ordinary income.

nodes.label: Hobby gambler — not a business
nodes.body: If your gambling lacks the characteristics of a business — infrequent or casual betting, no system or organisation, motive is recreation rather than profit — the activity is a hobby. A mere hobby punter's winnings are a windfall, not ordinary income (Brajkovich).

cases.note: Brajkovich — hobby punter; winnings not assessable as they were not ordinary income and not the product of a business

nodes.label: Hobby: winnings are not assessable income
nodes.body: Winnings from hobby gambling are a windfall gain, not income according to ordinary concepts. They are not derived from any business, employment, or income-producing activity, and therefore are not included in assessable income under s 6-5. Prizes and awards may also be non-assessable depending on their character.

nodes.label: Hobby: losses are not deductible — s 8-1(2)(b) private/domestic exclusion
nodes.body: Gambling losses incurred by a hobby gambler are of a private or domestic nature and therefore cannot be deducted under s 8-1. Section 8-1(2)(b) expressly excludes losses or outgoings of a private or domestic nature. Since the losses are not incurred in gaining or producing assessable income or in carrying on a business, they are not deductible.

nodes.label: Hobby gambler — no income tax consequences from gambling
nodes.body: As a hobby gambler, your winnings are not assessable income and your losses are not deductible. There are no net income tax implications from your gambling activities, although you must still declare any other assessable income.
